title: Do Backlinks Still Matter for AI Search? Real Data Inside
excerpt: Do backlinks still matter for AI search? Real data from a 75,000-brand study shows what actually drives citations in ChatGPT and AI Overviews.
author: Umaira Liaquat
content:
Last updated: August 2026

A growing number of business owners are asking their SEO agency some version of the same question this year: if ChatGPT and Google's AI Overviews are answering searches directly, is link building still worth paying for? Do backlinks still matter for AI search, or has the entire game changed underneath everyone? The honest answer, backed by real published research rather than guesswork, is yes — but not in exactly the way backlinks mattered for classic Google rankings, and understanding that difference changes what you should actually be building.

This guide breaks down what the current data actually shows, why AI engines choose the sources they cite, and what that means for how you should be spending a link building budget in 2026.

The Headline Finding: Mentions Beat Links, But Links Aren't Dead

Ahrefs analyzed 75,000 brands to see what actually correlates with a brand's visibility in Google's AI Overviews. The result surprised a lot of SEOs: branded web mentions correlated with AI Overview visibility at 0.664, while traditional backlinks correlated at only 0.218 — roughly three times weaker as a signal.

That doesn't mean backlinks stopped mattering. It means AI systems are weighing something broader than a raw link graph: how often and in what context your brand gets talked about across the web, whether or not every mention includes a clickable link. A backlink is still one of the strongest individual signals available, but it now competes with unlinked mentions, forum discussions, and review-site citations for the same job — convincing an AI model that your brand is a credible answer to a question. The full breakdown is worth reading directly in Ahrefs' original correlation study.

How Different AI Engines Actually Pick Their Sources

The three major AI answer engines don't source citations the same way, which matters for where you focus link building effort.

Google AI Overviews and Gemini pull heavily from Google's own index and favor content with strong E-E-A-T signals. Research on AI Overview citation patterns has found that a majority of the links cited in AI Overviews come from high-authority domains — and Reddit and Quora show up disproportionately often, reflecting how much weight community discussion carries.

ChatGPT blends its training data with live search results when browsing is active, and shows a clear preference for expert blogs, industry publications, and Wikipedia-style reference content. A notable pattern in the data: a substantial share of ChatGPT's cited links come from business and service sites that don't even rank in Google's top 20 for the equivalent query — meaning ChatGPT is evaluating relevance and authority somewhat independently of classic SERP position.

Perplexity leans hardest toward specialist and analytical sources: review platforms, industry reports, and practitioner-written content over generic marketing pages.

What Kind of Links Still Move the Needle

Not every backlink carries the same weight in an AI-search world, and the gap between useful and useless links has widened.

Editorial links from expert-adjacent sources outperform everything else. A link earned inside a genuine comparison article, industry report, or expert roundup does two jobs at once: it passes traditional authority and it places your brand inside exactly the kind of "trusted context" AI models look for when deciding who to cite.

Placement inside the actual content matters more than ever. Links embedded naturally within an article's main body consistently outperform links sitting in a footer or an author bio — a pattern consistent with how these systems parse a page for genuinely relevant context rather than treating every link on a page as equal.

Directory submissions and low-effort link farms are close to worthless here. They were already flagged as low-value link schemes under Google's own spam policies; for AI citation purposes, a link with no surrounding editorial context or topical relevance gives a language model almost nothing to work with.

Repetition and co-citation compound. A brand that shows up once in a random blog post is a weak signal. A brand that shows up repeatedly across comparison articles, industry write-ups, and community threads — especially alongside recognized competitors — reads to an AI model as a genuine category player, not a one-off mention.

Why This Changes How You Should Build Links in 2026

The practical shift is less about abandoning link building and more about widening what counts as a worthwhile placement.

A backlink strategy built entirely around directories and generic guest posts was already the weakest version of link building before AI search existed. Now it's actively behind the curve, because it produces exactly the kind of thin, disconnected mentions that neither Google's classic algorithm nor an AI citation model finds convincing.

The stronger approach layers three things: genuine editorial backlinks from topically relevant, expert-adjacent sites; unlinked brand mentions in comparison content, reports, and forums, which now carry real weight even without a clickable link; and consistency, so your brand keeps appearing across the same industry conversations rather than in a single burst of activity.

None of this replaces the fundamentals — a link from a respected, relevant site remains one of the best investments in SEO. It simply means the definition of a "good placement" has expanded to include content and context that wouldn't have been tracked as a link building win two years ago. The same editorial-over-bulk principle holds across every industry we've covered, including our guide to link building for HVAC companies.

How to Check Whether Your Links Are Actually Working for AI Search

Rankings alone no longer tell the full story. A page can sit in Google's top three and still be invisible in ChatGPT or Perplexity's answers for the same topic. The most direct way to check is manual: ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode the actual questions your customers would ask, and see whether your brand appears, and which competitors get cited instead.

Tools built specifically for this — tracking brand mentions and citations across AI platforms rather than just keyword rank — have emerged rapidly over the past year as this gap became obvious to marketers. Whichever method you use, the metric that matters is citation frequency across real queries, not backlink count in isolation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do backlinks still matter for AI search visibility?

Yes, but less than they used to relative to brand mentions. Ahrefs' analysis of 75,000 brands found branded web mentions correlate with AI Overview visibility at 0.664, versus 0.218 for backlinks — roughly three times weaker. Backlinks still help, but they're now one signal among several rather than the dominant one.

What matters more for AI search: backlinks or brand mentions?

Brand mentions currently show a stronger statistical correlation with AI Overview visibility than backlinks do. That doesn't make backlinks irrelevant — a link from a high-authority, topically relevant site is still valuable — but an unlinked mention in the right context can now carry real weight too.

Do ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews cite the same kind of sources?

No. Google AI Overviews leans on Google's own index and favors high-authority domains along with community sites like Reddit and Quora. ChatGPT shows a notable preference for expert blogs and industry publications, and often cites business sites that don't rank in Google's top 20 for the same query. Perplexity favors specialist and analytical sources.

Are directory links still worth building for AI search?

Generic, low-context directory links carry very little weight for AI citation purposes. They lack the surrounding editorial content that helps an AI model understand why your brand is relevant to a topic. They can still help with basic local citation consistency, but they shouldn't be treated as a meaningful AI-visibility strategy on their own.

Where should link building anchor text and placement go for AI search?

Links embedded naturally within the main body of an article consistently outperform links placed in a footer or an author bio. Research on ChatGPT's citation patterns has found that a majority of cited links come from substantive content sections, not peripheral page elements.

Can a page rank well on Google but still be invisible in ChatGPT?

Yes, and this is increasingly common. Ranking position in Google and citation likelihood in an AI-generated answer are measured differently. A page can hold a strong Google position while still being skipped by ChatGPT or Perplexity in favor of a source those models weigh differently.

How do I know if my backlinks are helping with AI search specifically?

Ask the AI platforms directly. Query ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode with the real questions your customers would ask, and check whether your brand is cited and how it compares to competitors. Backlink count alone doesn't answer this question — actual citation frequency does.

Should I stop building backlinks and focus only on brand mentions?

No. The data shows mentions correlate more strongly, but the strongest position combines both: genuine editorial backlinks from relevant, authoritative sources, plus consistent unlinked mentions across comparisons, reports, and community discussion. Treating them as separate, either-or strategies misses how AI models actually evaluate credibility.

Does link building still make sense to pay for in the AI search era?

Yes, provided the links are genuinely editorial and topically relevant rather than bulk directory or PBN placements. Those bulk tactics were already weak for classic SEO and are close to worthless for AI citation purposes. Quality, contextual link building remains one of the better investments available.

title: Top 3 Link Building Agencies in Medellín — Verified 2026
excerpt: Top 3 link building agencies in Medellín, hand-verified for 2026 — real teams, real websites, no paid-link sellers included.
author: Umaira Liaquat
content:
Last updated: August 2026

Search for a link building agency in Medellín and Google's own AI Overview will hand you a mixed bag — genuine local SEO teams sitting right next to services that openly advertise "how to buy backlinks in Colombia." That distinction matters more than almost anything else on this list, because bought links are exactly the kind of shortcut Google's own spam policies penalize. Rather than repeating whatever a directory or an AI summary surfaces, every agency below was checked by hand: does the company's own website actually load, does it name real people, and does it practice what it sells.

Two agencies that appeared in early research were dropped before this list was finalized — one because its own website returned nothing but an error page, and one because its entire homepage was built around selling paid link placements, the opposite of what a legitimate link building service should look like.

Why Medellín's Market Is Worth Understanding First

Colombia had 41.7 million internet users at the end of 2025, putting internet penetration at 77.8% of the population, and social media reached 37.7 million user identities — 70.4% of the country. Medellín specifically has spent the last decade rebuilding its international reputation around technology and innovation, and that shift shows up directly in its digital agency scene: a meaningful share of the companies working there today are SEO- and link-building-first shops rather than general ad agencies that added "digital" to their service list.

LinkedIn's advertising reach in Colombia grew 20% year-over-year through late 2025 — faster than most other platforms in the market, — which tracks with Medellín's growing B2B and technology sector, exactly the kind of business that searches for a link building partner rather than a general marketing agency. Colombia's ecommerce sector is also projected to grow at a 7.28% compound annual rate from 2025 to 2029, per the U.S. International Trade Administration's country commercial guide, which is pulling in agencies with genuine backlink-acquisition expertise rather than just social media management.

That growth has also pulled in link sellers dressed up as agencies. Before comparing the three below, it's worth naming the difference plainly: a link building agency earns placements through outreach, guest content, and digital PR; a link seller simply rents space in a network of sites it already controls. The first is what Google's own guidance describes as legitimate; the second is a link scheme, full stop. The internet-use and platform-growth figures cited above come from DataReportal's Digital 2026: Colombia report.

Quick Comparison

Agency Specialty Founded / Size Pricing Model
SeologyFull-service SEO with dedicated link building2018 · team across 16 countriesMonthly retainer
Agencia de Marketing Digital AMDFull-service digital marketing, link building included in SEO~2007 · 60+ specialists, 6 officesMonthly retainer
Simbionte MarketingLead-generation-focused SEO for small businessesSmall team (1–10) · Medellín-nativeProject + retainer

Pricing models above are general patterns based on each agency's positioning and public information, not confirmed rate cards — always request a direct quote scoped to your project.

1. Seology

Seology (Agencia Seology) has operated out of Medellín since 2018 and has grown into one of the more established SEO-first shops in the city, reporting more than 250 clients positioned across 16 countries in Latin America. The agency is led by a named team — Felipe Uribe as CEO, Sebastián Restrepo as CTO, and Julián Durango as SEO Director — and lists Link Building as a distinct core service alongside on-page, technical, and content SEO, rather than folding it into a vague "digital marketing" bundle.

What stands out on Seology's own site is how explicitly it brands its methodology as white-hat: "only techniques approved by Google, sustainable growth with no risk of penalties" appears as one of its stated differentiators, not just a line buried in an FAQ. Reported clients include the Pontificia Universidad Javeriana and Essity's Tena brand, and case studies on the site cite specific growth figures — a claimed 292% organic traffic increase over five years for one Colombian ecommerce client — that are worth verifying directly with the agency rather than taking at face value, standard practice with any self-reported case study.

Best fit for: businesses that want link building handled inside a broader, structured SEO program by a team with a multi-country track record, rather than a standalone outreach service.

Pricing: typically a monthly retainer scoped to the SEO program as a whole, consistent with a full-service agency of this size.

2. Agencia de Marketing Digital AMD

AMD is the largest agency on this list by footprint, with a Medellín headquarters on Avenida Las Palmas alongside offices in Bogotá, Cali, Miami, Orlando, New York, and Panama City. The agency describes more than 20 years transforming brands, a team of 60-plus marketing professionals, and certified partner status with Google, HubSpot, and Meta — credentials that require ongoing recertification, not a one-time badge.

Link building at AMD sits inside its broader SEO service rather than standing alone: the agency describes building "high-quality links" as part of positioning content according to real search intent, alongside keyword research and on-page and off-page optimization. That structure suits a business that wants one team accountable for the whole SEO picture rather than coordinating a separate link building vendor against an in-house or other agency's content work.

Best fit for: mid-size to larger businesses that want SEO and link building handled by one accountable, full-service team with a genuine multi-city presence across Colombia and into the US.

Pricing: monthly retainer, typically scaled to the scope of services bundled in alongside link building.

3. Simbionte Marketing

Simbionte Marketing is the smallest and most Medellín-native of the three, based in the Pilarica neighborhood with a lean team built around what it calls its "SEED" methodology — research, strategy design, implementation, launch, and iteration, in that order, before scaling anything further. Rather than positioning SEO as a standalone deliverable, Simbionte frames its entire offering around lead capture, CRM management, and conversion, with search visibility as the entry point rather than the end goal.

That focus on lead systems over vanity rankings is a genuinely different pitch from the two larger agencies above, and its size cuts both ways: a five-person or smaller team means more direct access to the people doing the work, but a narrower bench if a project needs to scale quickly across many pages or markets at once.

Best fit for: small and medium Medellín businesses that want SEO treated as one part of a lead-generation system, not an isolated ranking project, and that value working directly with a small, local team.

Pricing: typically project-based for the initial SEED diagnostic and strategy, moving to an ongoing retainer once implementation begins.

How These Agencies Were Chosen

Every agency on this list needed to clear three checks: a working, reachable website with real content (not a directory listing alone), a named team or leadership rather than an anonymous storefront, and a business model built around earning links through outreach and content rather than selling placements in an owned network. Two candidates that came up in initial research through Google's AI Overview and third-party directories like Clutch and The Manifest were dropped during verification — one whose own domain returned only an error page across repeated attempts, and one whose homepage was explicitly built around "how to buy backlinks in Colombia," a service model that conflicts directly with white-hat SEO practice regardless of how it's marketed. Team sizes, founding years, and client names are drawn from each agency's own published materials and third-party business profiles, and are noted as such rather than presented as independently audited.

How These 3 Agencies Compare

  • Most established, multi-country reach: Seology's 250-plus clients across 16 countries make it the strongest pick for a business that wants proof of scale beyond the Medellín market alone.
  • Broadest full-service footprint: AMD's six-city presence across Colombia, the US, and Panama suits a business that wants one team handling SEO alongside web design, ads, and social media.
  • Most boutique and locally rooted: Simbionte's small team and lead-generation-first framing fits a smaller business that wants direct access and a system built around conversions, not just rankings.

What Pricing Typically Looks Like

None of the three agencies above publish flat public pricing, which is standard across the industry — scope, competitiveness of the target keywords, and how much content and outreach a project needs all move the number too much for a single published rate to mean anything. That said, the general pattern across established Medellín agencies holds: full-service shops like Seology and AMD price link building as part of a broader monthly SEO retainer scoped to deliverables, while a smaller, lead-focused shop like Simbionte is more likely to start with a project-based diagnostic before moving to an ongoing retainer once a system is in place.

Whatever the structure, the more useful question isn't the headline price but what's included at that price: how many links per month, from what kind of sites, with what reporting cadence. An agency that can't answer that specifically — regardless of how competitive its quote looks — is worth treating with caution.

What to Check Before Signing With Any of Them

  • Ask exactly how links are earned — outreach, guest content, and digital PR are legitimate; "our network" or a guaranteed link count for a flat fee usually means a private blog network or paid placement scheme
  • Check the sites they've placed links on for real, relevant content and real traffic — not just a domain rating number, which can be manipulated
  • Native Spanish-speaking strategists who understand Medellín and Colombian search behavior specifically, not a generic Latin American Spanish template
  • Clear ownership of your website, analytics, and Search Console — none of it should be held hostage to keep you on a contract
  • A realistic timeline — link building compounds over three to six months at minimum; anyone promising a specific ranking within weeks is selling, not advising

The Bottom Line

Medellín's digital agency scene has grown alongside the city's own reputation shift toward technology and innovation, and that has produced genuinely capable SEO and link building teams — but it has also produced link sellers using the same marketing language. Seology, AMD, and Simbionte each cover a meaningfully different need: multi-country scale, full-service breadth, or a lean lead-generation-first system, and the right choice depends more on which of those matches your business than on picking whichever name appears first in a generic search.

Whichever agency you consider, the due diligence doesn't change: ask how links are actually earned, request to see real recent placements, and confirm in writing who owns your website and analytics access once the relationship ends. A genuinely legitimate agency answers all three without hesitation.

Related Reading

  • For the wider Latin American context, see our guide to digital marketing agencies in Mexico, which covers how Spanish-language search behavior shifts market to market.
  • For a broader look at how link building tactics translate across industries, see our guide to link building for HVAC companies.
What are the top link building agencies in Medellín?

Three agencies passed a hand-verification check for 2026: Seology, Agencia de Marketing Digital AMD, and Simbionte Marketing. Each suits a different type of business — multi-country scale, full-service breadth, or a small lead-generation-focused team — rather than there being one universal best.

How much does link building cost in Medellín?

None of the agencies above publish flat rates. Full-service agencies typically price link building inside a broader monthly SEO retainer, while smaller shops may start with a project-based diagnostic before moving to a retainer. Always ask what's included — link volume, site quality, reporting — rather than comparing headline prices alone.

How do I know if a Medellín link building agency is legitimate?

Check that their own website loads and shows real content, ask specifically how they earn links (outreach and content, not "a network"), and verify any named team members and clients independently. Be highly cautious of any agency whose own marketing describes buying or selling backlinks directly.

Is buying backlinks in Colombia safe for SEO?

No. Paid links that pass ranking authority without proper disclosure violate Google's spam policies and risk a manual penalty or algorithmic devaluation. Some Medellín-adjacent services market themselves openly around "buying backlinks" — that framing alone is a reason to avoid them regardless of price.

Why is Medellín a growing hub for digital agencies?

Medellín has spent roughly the last decade building a reputation around technology and innovation, which has attracted both genuine SEO specialists and a wider pool of digital marketing talent. Colombia's broader internet penetration (77.8% as of late 2025) and growing ecommerce sector have supported that growth.

Should I hire a Medellín agency or a remote specialist?

Either can work well. A Medellín-based team often has a natural advantage in understanding local search behavior and business culture, but what matters most is whether the agency has native Spanish-speaking strategists and a transparent, white-hat link building process, regardless of location.

How long does link building take to show results in Colombia?

Similar to most markets: initial technical and citation fixes can show movement within weeks, while competitive keyword rankings built through earned links typically take three to six months of consistent work to show meaningful movement.

What's the difference between link building and buying backlinks?

Link building earns placements through outreach, guest content, or digital PR on sites that publish for their own genuine audience. Buying backlinks pays for placement in a network the seller already controls, which Google's spam policies treat as a link scheme regardless of how it's marketed.

Do these agencies work with businesses outside Medellín?

Yes. Seology reports clients across 16 countries, and AMD operates offices across Colombia, the US, and Panama. Simbionte is the most locally focused of the three, though its services aren't restricted to Medellín-based clients.

Can a small business afford professional link building in Medellín?

Yes, though the structure differs by agency size. Smaller, boutique agencies like Simbionte are generally more accessible to smaller budgets through project-based work, while full-service agencies typically require a larger monthly retainer given their broader scope.

title: Link Building for HVAC: 9 Tactics That Fill the Schedule
excerpt: Link building for HVAC companies explained: 9 tactics — manufacturer directories, utility listings, seasonal press — that lift local rankings.
author: Umaira Liaquat
content:
Last updated: August 2026

An HVAC business lives and dies by two brutal spikes a year — the first heat wave and the first cold snap — and by the time either hits, it is too late to start building the online authority that decides who gets found first. Link building for HVAC companies is the off-season work that pays off exactly when demand peaks, because Google uses backlinks as one of its clearest signals of which local sites to trust before the calls start flooding in.

This guide covers the tactics unique to heating and cooling contractors — several of which are not available to most other trades — along with what a quality link actually costs and the mistakes that get HVAC sites penalized.

Why Link Building for HVAC Companies Rewards Patience

Backlinks influence rankings because they signal a website's authority to search engines — sometimes called Domain Rating or Domain Authority depending on which tool measures it. Not every link helps: black-hat tactics can actively penalize or de-index a heating and cooling site, while genuine, relevant links compound over time. Three factors decide whether a specific backlink is worth having: the authority of the linking site, how relevant that site is to HVAC or home services, and whether the anchor text looks natural rather than manipulated. A link from a trusted local newspaper moves the needle; a link from an unrelated low-quality blog does close to nothing.

1. Claim Your Manufacturer Dealer Locator Listings

This is the single highest-value tactic most HVAC companies never claim. If you install equipment from Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman, or any major manufacturer, you are almost certainly eligible for a listing in their "find a dealer" or "find a contractor" locator. These are high-authority manufacturer domains linking directly to certified local installers, and Google treats them as strong, industry-relevant endorsements — a category of link most other local trades simply do not have access to.

Check every brand you install or service and confirm your certification status is current. It is common for HVAC companies to hold two or three eligible certifications and have claimed none of the directory listings that come with them.

2. Get Listed on Utility and Rebate Program Directories

This tactic is close to unique to HVAC and a handful of adjacent trades. Local utility companies and energy-efficiency programs maintain directories of certified or participating contractors for rebate-eligible installations — heat pumps, high-efficiency furnaces, smart thermostats. Getting listed as a certified contractor with your regional utility, or through a program like ENERGY STAR's certified partner network, earns a link from a genuinely high-authority, government-adjacent source that most competitors overlook entirely.

3. Build Local Citations With Perfectly Consistent NAP

Claim and fully complete Google Business Profile first, then Bing Places and Apple Maps. From there, work through the core local directories — Yelp, Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack, and the Better Business Bureau. Keep your business name, address, and phone number identical across every single listing; inconsistent NAP data confuses Google's local-pack algorithm and quietly suppresses map visibility even when every other signal is strong.

4. Partner With Non-Competing Local Trades

Plumbers, electricians, and insulation contractors serve an overlapping customer base without competing directly for HVAC work, which makes them natural link and referral partners. A simple cross-mention arrangement — you link to their service page from a relevant blog post, they do the same for you — produces exactly the kind of contextual, genuinely relevant link Google's guidelines describe as valuable rather than manipulative. These partnerships also generate real referral business alongside the backlink.

5. Sponsor Local Events and Community Organizations

Sponsoring a youth sports team, a charity drive, or a community festival typically earns a link from the organizer's sponsors page, along with genuine local visibility. Always ask directly for the URL and business name when confirming a sponsorship — it is rarely automatic but rarely refused when requested. These links carry particular weight for HVAC because they are unmistakably tied to a real, physical presence in the service area Google is trying to verify.

6. Create Data-Driven Content Worth Citing

The fastest way to earn links passively is to rank for the questions people actually search before hiring, then let other sites reference your answer. A page that directly and thoroughly answers "how much does a new AC unit cost" or "how often should HVAC filters be replaced" becomes something bloggers, local journalists, and comparison sites want to cite as a source. Original local data works even better — average service call response times, the most common repair calls in your area by season, or a breakdown of regional energy costs give local publications a concrete reason to link back.

7. Pitch Seasonal Tips to Local Press

Local newspapers and neighborhood blogs regularly need practical, timely content, and HVAC contractors have an obvious supply of it: winterizing tips before the first cold snap, AC efficiency advice before the first heat wave, or what to check before a holiday travel shutdown. Pitching a short, specific, useful tip to a local reporter or blog editor a few weeks before the seasonal shift routinely earns a link with far less effort than cold outreach to unrelated sites.

8. Pursue Guest Posts and Niche Edits on Home Blogs

A small number of genuine guest posts on home-improvement blogs, real estate sites, or property management publications add real editorial authority when the content is specific and useful — a guide to combi versus tankless water heaters, or what a home inspector actually checks in an HVAC system. Niche edits, where an existing relevant article adds a link to your resource instead of new content being written, can be faster and often carry strong authority because the host page already has its own established backlinks. Apply a quality floor to both: a domain rating of roughly 20 or higher and genuine monthly traffic, not just a willingness to publish anything for a fee.

9. Build Brand Recognition Before You Need the Link

Sites link more readily to businesses they already recognize, because it removes the credibility risk of sending their readers somewhere unfamiliar. Sharing your content consistently on social media, keeping business information current everywhere it appears, and being visibly active in your service area over months — not just during a single outreach push — makes every subsequent ask for a link an easier yes. Brand recognition is not a link-building tactic on its own, but it is the multiplier that makes every other tactic on this list work better.

Sequencing: What to Do First If You Are Starting From Zero

A brand-new HVAC business with no citations gets little value chasing manufacturer directory links before Google has any basic trust signals to work with. The realistic order starts with the foundation: complete Google Business Profile and the core citation platforms first, since Google needs to verify your identity and location before anything else pays off fully. Move to manufacturer and utility directory listings second — they double as citations and authority backlinks and typically require only an email confirming your certification. Sponsorships, trade partnerships, and press pitches come third, once the basics are solid, and content-led guest posting last, since it depends on having an established, credible site other publishers are comfortable linking to.

An HVAC company with years of consistent local presence can skip most of the early sequence and move straight into editorial outreach and content-led link building, where the authority gain per link is highest.

What to Avoid: Tactics That Trigger a Penalty

The HVAC SEO space attracts a steady supply of vendors selling bulk backlink packages, private blog network placements, and automated directory blasts — and the guides warning against these tactics are sometimes published by the very companies selling them elsewhere on their own site. Google's spam policies explicitly flag private blog networks, paid links without a rel="sponsored" tag, and irrelevant mass directory submissions as link schemes. Before hiring any link-building service, ask directly what sites they place links on, what minimum authority and traffic thresholds they apply, and whether you can see real examples — vague answers are the clearest warning sign.

What Quality HVAC Backlinks Cost

A single high-quality guest post or niche edit from a relevant, authoritative site typically runs $130–$250 depending on the site's authority and how competitive the niche is. Full-service agency programs covering outreach, content, and digital PR for an HVAC business generally run $1,500–$5,000+ per month. If a vendor offers a large batch of links for a price well below a single quality placement, assume those links will not help and may actively harm your rankings.

The manufacturer, utility, and citation work in this guide costs mainly time and is realistic to complete within a focused week or two. Guest posting, niche edits, and press outreach take more sustained effort, which is where many HVAC businesses bring in outside help while keeping local partnerships and sponsorships in-house.

How Long Before Link Building Moves HVAC Rankings

Citation and directory fixes tend to show local-pack movement within four to eight weeks, since Google verifies NAP data relatively quickly. Editorial links from manufacturers, utilities, and press take longer to compound — expect meaningful ranking movement over three to six months, with results building further after that. Link building for HVAC is not a one-off seasonal push; it is ongoing authority that keeps paying off through every future heat wave and cold snap, which is exactly why starting in the off-season is the advantage competitors who wait do not have. Manufacturer dealer locators are high-authority, industry-specific domains linking directly to certified installers, which is a category of link most other local trades cannot access. Google treats them as strong, relevant endorsements, and most eligible HVAC companies never claim the certifications they already qualify for.

There is no fixed number. Relevance and referring-domain diversity matter more than raw count — check what the top-ranking HVAC companies in your specific market have before setting a target, and prioritize a handful of genuinely relevant links over dozens of low-quality directory submissions.

How much does HVAC link building cost?

A single quality guest post or niche edit typically costs $130–$250. Full-service agency programs generally run $1,500–$5,000+ per month. Be cautious of bulk link packages priced well below a single quality placement — they usually signal spam that can harm rankings.

Are paid backlinks safe for an HVAC website?

Paid links that pass ranking authority without a rel="sponsored" tag violate Google's spam policies and risk a penalty. Safe spending looks different: sponsorships, association memberships, and professional outreach, where money buys the work and the relationship, not the link itself.

What are the best directories for HVAC contractors?

Start with Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack, and the Better Business Bureau, then add every manufacturer dealer locator you qualify for and your regional utility's certified contractor directory. Keep your NAP identical everywhere.

How long does HVAC link building take to show results?

Citation and directory fixes often show local-pack movement within four to eight weeks. Manufacturer, utility, and editorial links take longer to compound, typically producing meaningful ranking gains over three to six months, with results building further after that.

Why does the off-season matter for HVAC link building?

Link authority takes months to compound, and HVAC demand is sharply seasonal. Building citations, manufacturer listings, and editorial links during slower months means the authority is already in place before the first heat wave or cold snap drives peak search volume.

Can I do HVAC link building myself?

Yes — citations, manufacturer directories, utility listings, and sponsorships are entirely DIY-friendly and cost mainly time. Press outreach and guest posting take more sustained relationship-building, which is where many HVAC businesses bring in a specialist while keeping local partnerships in-house.

title: Link Building for Plumbers: 9 Tactics That Ring the Phone
excerpt: Link building for plumbers explained: 9 safe tactics — citations, association listings, guest posts — that lift local rankings and bring in calls.
author: Umaira Liaquat
content:
Last updated: August 2026

If your plumbing website isn't generating calls, the problem is rarely the site itself — it's usually authority. Google needs a reason to trust a page before it sends customers there, and the clearest signal it uses for that trust is backlinks: links from other sites pointing to yours. Link building for plumbers is how a plumbing business earns that trust deliberately, instead of hoping years of word-of-mouth eventually shows up in search rankings.

This guide covers what actually counts as a backlink versus a citation, nine tactics a real plumbing business can run safely, what quality links cost, and the shortcuts that get sites penalised instead of ranked.

Backlinks vs. Citations: The Distinction That Changes Your Strategy

A backlink is a hyperlink from another site that passes ranking authority to yours and lifts organic, blue-link results. A citation is any online mention of your business name, address, and phone number (NAP) — with or without a link — and it works mainly to confirm your identity and location for Google's local-pack algorithm, the map results that show up above organic listings for "plumber near me" searches.

A high-authority directory listing that includes your URL delivers both signals at once, which is why directories are almost always the right place to start. One critical rule applies across every listing: keep your NAP exactly consistent — same business name, same address format, same phone number, everywhere. Inconsistencies confuse Google's local algorithm and can quietly suppress your map-pack visibility.

Why This Matters More for Plumbers Than It Looks

A large-scale study of Google ranking factors by Backlinko puts a number on the gap most plumbers underestimate: pages sitting in the #1 spot carry roughly 3.8 times more backlinks on average than pages ranked two through ten. For a plumbing business competing against five or six similarly-built local sites, that referring-domain gap is very often the real tiebreaker deciding who gets the call.

Local intent sharpens this further. A large share of "plumber near me" and "[service] near me" searches come from someone with an active leak or an emergency, and Google's local-pack algorithm leans heavily on citation consistency and Google Business Profile completeness alongside backlinks to decide who appears first. A plumbing site with a thin, inconsistent web presence is effectively invisible to exactly the searches most likely to convert into a same-day job.

What Makes a Backlink Actually Valuable

Not every link is worth the same. Three factors decide whether a backlink helps or does nothing:

Relevance. A link from a home-improvement site or local news publication carries far more weight than one from a completely unrelated niche — Google evaluates the topical context around a link, not just its existence.

Traffic and authority. Links from sites that actually have visitors and a reasonable domain rating move rankings; links from sites nobody reads or visits do not. A rough quality floor worth using when evaluating any link opportunity is a domain rating of 20 or higher with at least 500 monthly organic visitors.

Placement and anchor text. A link embedded naturally within the body of an article outranks one buried in a footer or sidebar widget. Descriptive anchor text — "emergency plumber in [city]" or "local plumbing services" — helps search engines understand the linked page, but over-optimised, keyword-stuffed anchors across many links look manipulative rather than earned.

1. Claim the Core Local Citations First

For most plumbing businesses, this is the fastest and most straightforward starting point. Claim and fully complete Google Business Profile before anything else, then Bing Places and Apple Maps. From there, work through the major US directories: Yelp, Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack, and the Better Business Bureau. Most of these are free; paid options like Angi's featured placements can be worth it in competitive metros since they send referral traffic alongside the citation value.

2. Join the Plumbing-Heating-Cooling Contractors Association (PHCC)

PHCC and its state chapters maintain member directories with links — a trusted .org-adjacent source that functions as both a citation and an editorial-quality backlink simultaneously. If you hold any manufacturer certifications (Rheem Pro Partner, Moen Pro, Kohler-authorized dealer, and similar programs), check each one for a "find a contractor" or "preferred partner" locator. These are links most plumbers are entitled to and never claim, because they are not the first thing that comes to mind when someone says "backlinks."

3. Build Local Sponsorship and Community Links

These hyper-local links carry real weight for map-pack rankings because they signal to Google that a business is genuinely embedded in the area it serves — something no directory-spam vendor can fabricate. Sponsoring a local youth sports team, a charity event, or a school program typically earns a link from the organiser's sponsors page. Always ask directly for the URL and your business name when confirming a sponsorship; it is rarely offered automatically but rarely refused when requested.

4. Pursue Guest Posts and Niche Edits

Citations build a foundation, but competitive local search terms usually require editorial backlinks — links from genuine content on established sites. Two methods dominate here.

Guest posting means writing an article for a relevant site — home-improvement blogs, property management sites, landlord forums, local trade publications — and earning a backlink within genuinely useful content, such as a guide on preventing frozen pipes or what to check before calling a plumber.

Niche edits (also called link insertions) work differently: instead of writing new content, you find an existing relevant article and ask the site owner to add your link naturally within it. This is often faster than guest posting and can carry strong authority, since the page already has its own established backlinks.

For both, apply the same quality floor mentioned earlier — DR 20 minimum, real traffic, topical or geographic relevance. If someone offers fifty links for a flat low fee, that is a red flag, not a bargain.

5. Create Content Worth Linking To

Content earns links passively when it solves a real problem better than what already exists. For plumbing, that means specific, detailed guides homeowners actually search for — "how to know when your water heater needs replacing" or "what to do if your pipes freeze overnight" — written with real expertise rather than generic filler. Local data works even better: average callout response times, the most common emergency plumbing issues in your area, or seasonal spikes in specific jobs give local publications and bloggers a genuine reason to reference and link to your site.

Comparison content — a tankless versus traditional water heater breakdown, or an explanation of pipe material options — and a genuinely detailed FAQ page both tend to attract natural references over time. None of this replaces active outreach, but it makes outreach dramatically more effective once you have something worth linking to.

6. Reclaim Unlinked Brand Mentions

Search your business name in Google periodically. Local news write-ups, supplier newsletters, or community blog posts that mention your company without linking to it are one polite email away from becoming a backlink. This costs nothing beyond the time to search and ask, and it is one of the most overlooked tactics on this list.

Which Tactics Trigger a Google Penalty

The market is full of services offering large volumes of links at very low prices, and most of them either do nothing or actively damage rankings. Google's spam policies explicitly name the tactics to avoid: private blog networks built solely to pass authority, bulk directory spam, paid placements without a rel="sponsored" tag, and irrelevant mass submissions. When evaluating any link-building service, ask directly what sites they use, what minimum authority and traffic thresholds they apply, and whether links come from topically relevant sites or generic link farms.

The consequence ranges from a silent algorithmic devaluation to a manual "unnatural links" action in Search Console, which requires formal remediation before rankings recover. If a previous vendor left behind a toxic link profile, request removal from site owners first and disavow only the domains that cannot be removed.

What Quality Links Actually Cost

Effective link building is not cheap, and that is by design — the price reflects real editorial work, not just a line in a spreadsheet. A single high-quality guest post or niche edit from a relevant, authoritative site typically runs $130–$200 or more depending on the site's authority and niche competitiveness. Full-service agency programs covering outreach, content, and digital PR generally run $1,500–$5,000+ per month for a local trade business. If someone offers twenty links for the price of a single quality placement, assume those links will not help and may actively set back your rankings.

Doing the foundational work yourself — citations, association listings, sponsorship outreach — costs mainly time and is realistic for a busy owner to complete in a focused week. Guest posting and niche-edit outreach take more sustained effort and relationship-building, which is where many plumbing businesses bring in outside help.

Anchor Text and Pacing: Two Habits That Keep You Safe

Two technical details separate a link profile that looks natural from one that reads as engineered, because the difference between them is exactly what Google's algorithms are built to spot.

Anchor text is the clickable wording of a link. A healthy profile is dominated by brand anchors ("Smith Plumbing"), bare URLs, and natural phrases, with exact-match anchors like "emergency plumber [city]" kept to a small minority. When every link uses the exact keyword a business wants to rank for, it stops looking like something people chose to link to and starts looking like something engineered — because real websites and real customers simply do not link that way on their own.

Pacing matters just as much. A sudden burst of ten links after two years of none is a pattern every link-buying vendor produces, and Google has seen it thousands of times. Spread the work across months — citations this month, association listings the next, a sponsorship after that. Steady, deliberate growth is both safer and, conveniently, easier to sustain alongside actually running a plumbing business. The same logic holds for any local trade; our guide to link building for roofers covers the identical pacing principle from a different angle if you want to see how it plays out in another vertical.

How Long Link Building for Plumbers Takes to Work

Most plumbers see meaningful movement in local search rankings within three to six months of a consistent link-building effort. Competitive metros with dozens of established plumbing businesses take longer; smaller towns and specific service niches can move faster. The important thing to understand is that link building is cumulative — every quality link adds to your site's authority, and that authority compounds. A business that builds links consistently for a year becomes significantly harder for a new competitor to displace than one that runs a single burst campaign and stops. Think of it less as a campaign and more as a reputation you are building.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do plumbers get backlinks?

The most reliable sources are local citations and directories (Google Business Profile, Yelp, Angi, HomeAdvisor), industry association listings (PHCC, state chapters), manufacturer "preferred contractor" pages, local sponsorships, guest posts on home-improvement blogs, and niche edits on existing relevant articles.

What is the difference between a backlink and a local citation?

A backlink is a hyperlink that passes ranking authority and lifts organic search results. A citation is any online mention of your name, address, and phone number, with or without a link, and it mainly supports local-pack and map visibility. A directory listing with your URL provides both at once.

How many backlinks does a plumbing website need?

There is no fixed number — relevance and referring-domain diversity matter more than raw count. Check what the top-ranking plumbers in your specific market have before setting a target, and prioritise a handful of genuinely relevant links over dozens of low-quality directory submissions.

How much does link building cost for a plumbing business?

A single quality guest post or niche edit typically costs $130–$200 or more depending on site authority. Full-service agency programs generally run $1,500–$5,000+ per month. Be cautious of any offer well below these ranges — it usually signals bulk, low-quality links that can harm rather than help.

Are paid backlinks safe for a plumbing website?

Paid links that pass ranking authority without a rel="sponsored" tag violate Google's spam policies and risk a penalty. Safe spending looks different: sponsorships, association memberships, and professional outreach, where the money buys the relationship and the work, not the link itself.

What are the best directories for plumbers?

Start with Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack, and the Better Business Bureau. Add your state PHCC chapter and any manufacturer certification directories you qualify for. Keep your name, address, and phone identical across every listing.

How long does link building take to work for a plumbing site?

Most plumbers see meaningful local ranking movement within three to six months of consistent effort. Competitive metro markets typically take longer, while smaller towns and specific service niches can move faster. Results compound the longer a consistent effort continues.

What's the fastest link-building win for a new plumbing business?

Fully completing your Google Business Profile and claiming the core citation platforms (Yelp, Angi, HomeAdvisor, BBB) with perfectly consistent NAP data. This is free, fast, and gives Google the identity signals it needs before editorial backlinks can do their best work.

Can I remove backlinks a previous SEO vendor built badly?

Yes. Contact site owners and request removal first, documenting every attempt. For links that genuinely cannot be removed, submit a disavow file in Google Search Console listing only the spammy domains — disavowing healthy links by mistake can hurt rankings more than leaving toxic ones alone.

If you use a specific dental lab, equipment brand, or materials supplier regularly, ask whether they run a customer spotlight, preferred-provider list, or testimonials page. The realistic order is: complete every core citation first, claim the association and ADA directory listings second (they double as citations and backlinks), then move into sponsorships, supplier links, and digital PR once the foundation is solid.

If you are unsure which stage your practice is at, a quick citation audit against the shortlist above will tell you within an hour.

What Dental Link Building Actually Costs

Link building is not a one-off campaign; it is an ongoing signal that Google reassesses continuously, and the practices that keep a steady, modest pace outperform the ones that do a single push and stop.

Tracking Results Without Getting Lost in Vanity Metrics

Three numbers matter monthly: referring domains gained, rankings for your money keywords ("dentist in [city]", "[procedure] near me"), and — the one that actually pays the bills — new patient calls and form submissions traced back to organic search. Google Search Console's Performance report shows impressions and clicks by page; low impressions on a service page you have invested in usually points to a technical or indexing problem rather than a content one.

If referring domains are climbing but calls are not, the bottleneck is rarely the links themselves — it is usually the Google Business Profile setup or the website's booking flow. What is the difference between a backlink and a citation for a dental practice?

A backlink is a hyperlink that passes ranking authority and lifts organic search results. A citation is any online mention of your name, address, and phone number, with or without a link, and it mainly supports local-pack and map visibility. A high-authority directory listing with your URL provides both at once.

How many backlinks does a dental website need?

There is no fixed number. Referring-domain diversity and relevance matter more than raw count — dozens of relevant local and industry links typically outperform hundreds of low-quality directory submissions. Check what the top-ranking practices in your specific market have before setting a target.

How much does link building cost for a dental practice?

Individual quality placements typically cost $100–$400, with broader or niche-relevant placements running higher. Agency retainers for ongoing programs generally range from $3,000 to $15,000+ per month. Be wary of any vendor quoting a single flat price without knowing your market — that usually signals bulk, low-quality links.

Are paid backlinks safe for a dental website?

Paid links that pass ranking authority without a rel="sponsored" tag violate Google's spam policies and risk a manual penalty. Safe spending looks different: sponsorships, association memberships, and professional outreach, where money buys the relationship and the work, not the link itself.

What are the best directories for dentists?

Start with Google Business Profile, Apple Maps, Bing Places, and Yelp, then add Healthgrades, Zocdoc, WebMD, and Vitals. Layer in the ADA's Find-a-Dentist directory and your state or county dental society. Keep your name, address, and phone identical across every listing.

How long does dental link building take to show results?

Citation and directory fixes often show local-pack movement within four to eight weeks. Editorial and authority backlinks take longer to compound, typically producing meaningful ranking gains over three to six months, with results building further after that.

Can I remove toxic backlinks a previous SEO company built?

Yes. Contact the site owners and request removal first, documenting every attempt. For links that cannot be removed, submit a disavow file in Google Search Console listing only the genuinely spammy domains — disavowing healthy links by mistake can hurt rankings more than leaving toxic ones in place.

Does a dental practice need a blog to earn backlinks?

Not strictly, but it helps. A blog gives you a home for the linkable resources — guides, infographics, explainer videos — that local sites and journalists actually want to reference. Without one, most of your link opportunities are limited to citations, sponsorships, and directory listings.

title: Link Building for Roofers: 9 Tactics That Win Jobs (2026)
excerpt: Link building for roofers explained: 9 practical tactics — manufacturer directories, local press, sponsorships — that lift local rankings and win jobs.
author: Umaira Liaquat
content:
Last updated: August 2026

A roofing company two towns over is pulling thirty calls a month from Google while your phone stays quiet — and in most cases the difference is not their website design, their reviews, or even their prices. It is their backlink profile. Link building for roofers is the least understood part of roofing SEO, and that is exactly why it works: most of your competitors are not doing it at all.

This guide walks through nine tactics that actually fit a roofing business — no theory borrowed from tech blogs, no spam shortcuts that get sites penalised. Just the links that move local rankings and turn searches into booked jobs.

Why Backlinks Decide Which Roofer Ranks

When a homeowner searches “roof repair near me,” Google has to choose between dozens of local companies with similar services and similar websites. Backlinks are one of its strongest tiebreakers — every credible website that links to yours acts as a vote that your business is real, established, and trusted.

For roofers this matters twice over. Links influence your organic rankings for terms like “roof replacement [your city],” and the authority they build also feeds the signals behind the local map pack, where the highest-intent customers click. A roofing site with even 20–30 genuine local links routinely outranks competitors with none — because in most local roofing markets, almost nobody is building links deliberately.

That is the opportunity. Here are the nine tactics, ordered roughly by effort.

1. Claim the Core Citations First

Citations are business listings — and while not every one passes link authority, they are the foundation Google uses to verify you exist. Start with Google Business Profile, then Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, BBB, Angi, Houzz, HomeAdvisor, and Thumbtack.

Two rules make or break this step. First, your NAP — name, address, phone — must be identical everywhere, down to “St” versus “Street.” Inconsistent listings confuse Google and dilute the benefit. Second, complete every profile fully: photos of real jobs, service descriptions, service areas. A half-empty listing is a wasted listing.

2. Get the Manufacturer Links You Already Earned

This is the single most overlooked link source in roofing. If you are certified by a shingle manufacturer — GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred Contractor, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster — you are entitled to a listing in their “find a contractor” directory. These are high-authority manufacturer domains linking to local roofing sites, and Google treats them as strong industry-relevant endorsements.

Check every certification, supplier, and distributor relationship you have and ask each one: “Do you have a dealer or contractor locator I should be listed in?” Most roofers qualify for two or three of these links and have claimed none.

3. Join the Associations That List Members

The National Roofing Contractors Association, your state roofing association, and your local chamber of commerce all publish member directories with links. These cost membership fees you may already be paying — the link is free. Association links carry exactly the kind of trust signal Google wants to see from a legitimate local trade business, and the chamber link doubles as a local relevance signal for your city.

While you are at it, check adjacent trade groups: home builders associations, remodeling councils, and BNI-style networking chapters often maintain member pages too. Each one is a small, verifiable vote that your company is a real, established local business — and together they form a base layer of authority that spam-heavy competitors cannot copy.

4. Turn Storm Response Into Local Press

Local news sites are the strongest links most roofers can realistically earn. After major weather events, local reporters need expert sources: what homeowners should check, how to spot storm-chaser scams, when to call insurance. Email the newsroom a short, useful comment within a day of the event and you will be surprised how often it becomes a quote — with a link.

Outside storm season, community stories work the same way: donating a roof to a veteran or a family in need, sponsoring a school fundraiser, training apprentices. One genuine community story a year can earn more authority than fifty directory listings.

5. Sponsor Things Your Customers Actually See

Local sponsorships — youth sports teams, charity runs, county fairs, trade school programs — almost always come with a link from the organisation's sponsors page. These are real local links Google can verify against a real local business, and unlike most tactics on this list, they also put your name in front of homeowners directly. Budget a few hundred dollars a season and collect both the goodwill and the backlink.

6. Answer Expert Queries on Featured.com

Journalists writing about home improvement constantly need contractor quotes. Platforms like Featured.com (which absorbed the old HARO service) match those requests with experts. Answer two or three roofing-related queries a week — cost of a roof replacement, insurance claims, seasonal maintenance — and over a few months you will land quotes in national and regional publications, many with links to your site.

The trick is speed and specificity: answer within hours, give a concrete number or example from a real job, and keep it under 150 words.

7. Guest Post on Home-Improvement Blogs (Selectively)

A handful of genuine guest posts on real home-improvement and real-estate blogs are worth having: a piece on “what a roof inspection actually covers” for a home-buying blog, or “preparing your roof for winter” for a homeowner site. The word that matters is real — the blog should have an actual audience, actual editorial standards, and content beyond guest posts. If a site publishes anything for $30, its links are worthless at best. Write two or three excellent pieces a year rather than twenty cheap ones.

8. Build One Linkable Asset for Your Market

Give local bloggers, agents, and news sites a reason to link to you. The assets that work for roofing are practical and local: a roof replacement cost breakdown for your metro area with real price ranges, a hail-damage photo guide showing what claims adjusters look for, or a post-storm inspection checklist homeowners can download. One genuinely useful local resource earns links passively for years — and positions you as the authority reporters call next time.

9. Reclaim Links From Broken Pages and Mentions

Two quick wins to run quarterly. First, search your company name in Google: anywhere you are mentioned without a link — a supplier newsletter, a local blog, a news story — is one polite email away from a backlink. Second, if you have ever changed domains or deleted old pages, links pointing at those dead URLs are being wasted; redirect the old URLs to the matching live pages and the authority flows back.

What to Avoid: The Shortcuts That Backfire

Roofing is a prime target for link sellers, and most of what they sell will hurt you. Avoid Fiverr link packages, private blog networks, comment spam, and “100 backlinks for $50” offers — these leave a footprint Google identifies and discounts, and in bad cases they trigger penalties that take months to recover from. Google's own guidance on link schemes is published in Google Search Central, and it is blunt: paid links that pass ranking credit violate their policies.

The test for any link opportunity is simple: would this link make sense if Google did not exist? A manufacturer directory, a chamber page, a news quote — yes. A casino blog linking to a roofer — no.

How Many Links Does a Roofing Site Need?

Less than you think. Most local roofing markets are decided by the difference between zero deliberate links and thirty good ones. A realistic benchmark: pull up the top three ranking roofers in your city in a backlink tool and count their referring domains. In most markets outside major metros, the leaders have 40–150 referring domains — a gap you can close in six to twelve months with the tactics above.

Quality beats volume at every step. One link from your local newspaper outweighs fifty directory submissions.

What It Costs and How Long It Takes

Doing this yourself costs mostly time: citations and manufacturer links are a one-week project, and press, sponsorships, and expert quotes are an hour or two a week ongoing. Hiring a specialist agency for roofing link building typically runs $500–$2,000 per month depending on market competitiveness — and is worth considering when jobs are worth thousands and page-one competitors are entrenched.

Expect early citation-driven movement within four to eight weeks, and meaningful ranking gains from authority links over three to six months. Link building compounds: the authority you build this year keeps ranking you next year, which is the opposite of paid ads that stop the moment the budget does.

Anchor Text and Pacing: Two Details That Protect You

Two technical habits keep a growing link profile looking natural, because it is natural.

Anchor text is the clickable wording of a link. A healthy roofing profile is dominated by brand anchors (“Smith Roofing”), bare URLs, and generic phrases (“this roofing company”), with exact-match anchors like “roof replacement dallas” kept rare. When every link says your money keyword, it reads as manipulation — real people simply do not link that way. You control anchor text directly in guest posts and directory bios, so spend that control on brand anchors.

Pacing matters just as much. Ten links appearing in a week after two years of none is a pattern Google has seen from every link buyer. Spread the work: citations this month, manufacturer directories the next, a sponsorship the month after. Steady beats sudden, and conveniently, steady is also easier to sustain alongside actual roofing work.

Link Building for Roofers: Your First 90 Days

If you are starting from zero, here is the sequence that gets the most authority for the least effort:

Weeks 1–2: Fix your NAP everywhere it appears, complete Google Business Profile fully, and claim the core citations from tactic one.

Weeks 3–4: Email every manufacturer, supplier, and association you have a relationship with about their contractor directories. This is usually the highest-authority win of the whole plan.

Weeks 5–8: Set up a Featured.com profile and answer two queries a week. Pick one local sponsorship for the coming season.

Weeks 9–12: Publish one linkable asset — a local cost guide or storm checklist — and email it to five local blogs, agents, or news contacts who cover housing in your area.

By day 90 you will typically have 15–25 new referring domains, all of them the kind that age well. From there, maintenance is a few hours a month.

Track What Matters

Measure three things monthly: referring domains (is the number growing?), rankings for your money keywords (“roof replacement [city]”, “roofing contractor [city]”), and — most importantly — calls and form fills from organic search. Rankings are the means; booked jobs are the result. If links are growing but calls are not, the problem is usually your Google Business Profile or your website's conversion path, not the link building. For deeper strategy on how outreach-based campaigns scale across markets, see our guide to multilingual link building.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do roofers get backlinks?

The most reliable sources are manufacturer certification directories (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed), industry and chamber memberships, local citations, local press quotes after storm events, community sponsorships, expert-quote platforms like Featured.com, and a small number of genuine guest posts on home-improvement blogs.

Do backlinks really help roofing SEO?

Yes. Backlinks are among Google's strongest trust signals, influencing both organic rankings and the authority behind local map pack results. Because most local roofers build no links deliberately, even 20–30 quality links often create a decisive ranking advantage.

How many backlinks does a roofing website need?

Check the top three ranking roofers in your market and count their referring domains — in most non-metro markets that is 40–150. Closing that gap with quality links typically takes six to twelve months. Quality matters far more than quantity.

What are the best directories for roofing companies?

Start with Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, BBB, Angi, Houzz, HomeAdvisor, and Thumbtack, then add your chamber of commerce, state roofing association, and NRCA member directory. Keep your name, address, and phone identical across all of them.

How much does link building cost for a roofing company?

Doing it yourself costs mainly time. Specialist agencies typically charge $500–$2,000 per month depending on market competitiveness. Be wary of anyone dramatically cheaper — bulk link packages are usually spam that can harm your rankings.

Are paid backlinks safe for roofers?

Links bought purely to pass ranking credit violate Google's spam policies and risk penalties. Safe spending looks different: association memberships, sponsorships, and professionally executed outreach — where money buys the work and the relationship, not the link itself.

How long does link building take to work for a roofing site?

Citation-driven improvements often appear within four to eight weeks. Authority links from press, manufacturers, and guest posts typically move competitive rankings over three to six months, with gains compounding after that.

Can I do roofing link building myself?

Yes — citations, manufacturer directories, associations, and sponsorships are entirely DIY-friendly. Press outreach and content-driven links take more skill and consistency, which is where many roofers bring in a specialist while keeping the local relationships themselves.

What anchor text should roofing backlinks use?

Mostly your brand name, your bare URL, and natural phrases. Keep exact-match keyword anchors like “roof repair [city]” to a small minority of links — profiles dominated by money-keyword anchors are a classic manipulation signal Google discounts or penalises.

Do social media links count as backlinks?

Social profiles and posts are typically nofollow, so they pass little direct ranking authority. They still matter for brand verification and visibility — complete profiles on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn support the trust picture Google builds around your business.

10 Questions to Ask an SEO Expert Before You Hire

But with dozens of agencies competing for your budget, choosing the right one is the hard part.

To make that easier, here are eight of the most frequently recommended SEO companies serving Kent, along with what each does best, the core services every agency should offer, and a proven checklist for choosing the right partner. This is a curated shortlist to research — not a rigid ranking — because the best agency for you depends entirely on your industry, goals, and budget.

How These Companies Were Chosen

Before the list, it’s worth knowing what genuinely separates a strong SEO agency from an average one. The providers below tend to score well on these points:

The best Kent SEO companies can show proof of past work through real case studies and measurable rankings, rather than vague promises. They offer transparent reporting, so you always know exactly what’s being done and how you’re performing. They take a full-stack approach that combines technical SEO, content, local optimisation, and link building into one coordinated plan. They set honest timelines instead of guaranteeing overnight results. And crucially, they’re clear about whether they focus on local or national reach — a distinction that matters enormously depending on your business model.

Keep these criteria in mind as you read, and use them when you interview any agency on this list.

1. Sleeping Giant Media

Sleeping Giant Media is one of the best-known digital agencies in Kent, based in Folkestone and widely recognised across the county. The team specialises in search marketing, combining organic SEO with paid advertising to build visibility across the whole search results page. They’re also known for their training and knowledge-sharing culture, which tends to translate into a well-educated client relationship.

Best for: Kent businesses that want both SEO and paid search handled by an established, well-regarded local team. You can explore their work at Sleeping Giant Media.

2. Reflect Digital

Reflect Digital, based in Maidstone, has built a strong reputation for blending data with consumer psychology — an approach they use to understand not just what people search for, but why. Alongside SEO, they’re active in digital PR, which is one of the most effective modern methods of earning the authoritative backlinks that drive rankings.

Best for: Brands that want a strategic, research-led approach and value digital PR as part of their SEO. Learn more via Reflect Digital.

3. Kayo Digital

Kayo Digital focuses on custom web builds paired with growth strategy, making it a natural fit for businesses whose websites need rebuilding as well as optimising. Because technical foundations and site structure have a direct impact on rankings, having the same team handle both your build and your SEO can remove a lot of friction.

Best for: Businesses that need a new or rebuilt website alongside a long-term SEO growth plan.

4. Improve My Search Ranking

Improve My Search Ranking offers SEO services with a notable emphasis on link building and driving measurable sales growth. Link building remains one of the most difficult and important parts of competitive SEO, so an agency that specialises in it can be valuable in tougher industries.

Best for: Businesses in competitive sectors that need serious authority building. See their Kent SEO agency page.

5. Level Up Leads

Level Up Leads works with small businesses on local search, helping them appear when nearby customers look for their services. For a small business, local visibility — particularly in Google’s map pack — is often the single highest-return marketing activity available.

Best for: Small and local Kent businesses focused on generating enquiries from their immediate area. Their agency roundup is at Level Up Leads.

Gooey Digital provides SEO as part of a broader digital services offering, working with businesses to improve search visibility alongside wider marketing support. 8. Compare More via Trusted Directories

Beyond the named agencies above, Kent and the wider South East have a deep bench of specialists and freelancers — and comparing several before committing is genuinely the smartest move.
